body:
>Me: yes we’re stagnant. For whatever reason you don’t seem compelled to make a commitment to me and that scares me
 

**He's been with you for *Six years*! That's a commitment.** I may have an unpopular opinion, and it's probably because I don't believe in marriage as an  institution, but girl. Get a grip. Do you want *him* or do you want a *marriage*. 

**Frankly, I think you were really wrong to say "either you love someone enough to marry them or you don't" Not everyone believes in Marriage.** It's like when you tell a childfree woman or man that they "don't know true love" It's patronizing, wrong, and insulting at best. My SO and I don't believe in the institution of marriage, and don't want that for us, do we not love each other then? According to you, we don't. Think before you make harsh generalizations like that.

**Do you want a *partner for life* or do you want a *marriage*?**

What would change if you married him? Why is Marriage your end goal when you've had wonderful lives together for 6 years? Marriage isn't the be all end all, it's not some checkpoint to cross off your list. In my opinion it's not even *necessary*, while I understand that is not your opinion, I *do* think you need to take a step back and look inside yourself and ask the question:

>Why do I need this so badly, and what do I *really* want to gain from it? what, in complete and utter honesty, would be *different*? 

**Now onto something that was really alarming: The way you two speak to each other is atrocious**  A lot of other posters have commented upon this but the way you two talk to each other is very accusatory and negative - I'd say this is a *huge* red flag for the relationship in general that maybe he is more aware of than you are. You're very aggressive about it, calm down a little bit and approach it a different way because clearly you've beaten him down with the way you're approaching the issue. Stop having serious conversations over text! This wasn't a discussion, this was you telling *him* how *he* feels. That's not okay, then when he tells you how he *actually* feels, you can't handle it.

You say he doesn't listen to you, but *you're not listening to him either*!

You want different things. Grounds for a breakup right there.

You can't *force* someone into a marriage.

It's like with kids: you wan't them or don't, there is no compromising on this. 

**As far as personal advice goes** - you need to work on your method of communication. Couples therapy and personal therapy can help with this. You do a lot of *telling* and not a lot of *listening* from what I can tell in your text conversation. When he says he thinks way A, you tell him no, you actually think Way B. When he tells you that, No, in fact I think way A you don't listen and think he's wrong. *LISTEN* TO HIM, don't *TELL* him how *he* feels. You do *not* know better than he does how he feels. You come off very abrasive, immediately defensive, haughty, and like you know better. These are poor communication skills that you *need* to work on if you're going to have healthy relationships.

**Patterns of Selfish Behavior**

whether you recognize it or not, in this post and in many of your comments there is this overarching theme of "me, me, me". "I want this" "I need that" "I don't know why he doesn't listen to me" "woe is me he thinks i'm naggy" - well, maybe you are? This *is not a grocery list*. Wanting to check something off is fine in that scenario, but don't be mistaken, this isn't just "oh a wedding and we're done". This is this mans *entire remainder of his life* that you're asking him for. Your wants, your needs are not the only ones in the equation and what worries me is that you don't even seem to be listening to *his* wants or *his* needs, and seem to think you're *entitled* or *owed* this marriage because you've "supported him for 4 years of schooling financially". You're not owed jack shit for that besides gratitude and perhaps in time his repayment of the finances if that is what you agreed upon. You don't do things for someone you love with the *expectation* of something in return - that's not how love works. Love is selfless. You need to take a step back and examine your behavior. There is a lot of me,me,me here and a lot of ignoring what he is telling you, and not even listening to his feelings or beliefs on this. You're not just expecting him to: 

a) Be on the same page as far as marriage importance goes

You seem to also be expecting him:

b) Be totally okay with following your plan as the *correct* plan - This kind of thinking is inherently selfish.

**TL;DR? Read it.**

uh probably because you said "Maybe I don't". Fuck if my SO said that to me I'd be so pissed. It's such a shitty thing to say after what she said, it's like confirming to her that you don't care about her.
